archetype.name: Pocket Passer (conservative)
archetype.definition: A tall, mostly stationary backup who wins only in the short and middle-of-the-field game from the pocket. When pressure arrives or the throw has to travel, he has little to fall back on.

report.headline: A checkdown backup who can't stretch defenses and takes too many sacks
report.take:
Tanner McKee has filled in for three games of an Eagles season that has already used three quarterbacks, two of them his official starts. The results have the shape of a classic QB2: volume without punch. He averages 212.7 passing yards a game, 15.8 above the qualifier average, but only 5.6 yards an attempt, 44th of 49. His -0.182 EPA per dropback sits 39th. The team lost all three games and failed to cover in any of them.

The profile is narrow. His aggressiveness is 14.91% and his average throw lands 2.84 yards short of the sticks. Under 10 air yards he completes 72.1% for roughly break-even EPA. When he does push it, the results split hard. Intermediate throws (0.253 EPA) and throws over the middle (0.45) have been his best football. The deep ball has been a disaster: 0-for-8 with an interception and -11.5 EPA, which by itself wipes out everything he gains short. Add a 31.3% pressure-to-sack rate and a pace of 57 sacks, and drives die on long third downs. He converts 28.6% of them, at an average of 9.4 yards to go.

The numbers flatter him in one place. When trailing by nine or more, he completes 70.7% with a +6.7 CPOE against soft, protect-the-lead coverage. In one-score games that collapses to 58.9% and -7.5, which is the truer read of the player. The inaccuracy is not new either. His bad-throw rate ranked 56th of 60 in 2024 and 62nd of 63 in 2025, and it sits 39th of 42 now. That sample is tiny, but the pattern is consistent. The excellent 2024 cameo (0.31 EPA per play) looks like the outlier, not the baseline.

The context hasn't helped. Philadelphia's offense ranks 29th in EPA, and the defense, 27th, keeps putting him in catch-up mode. Now DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are both out. He is listed as QB2 and was questionable with limited practice before Joe Milton III started Week 9. Whether he even plays again soon is an open question.

strengths.title: Accurate in the short area
strengths.body: Under 10 air yards he completes 72.1% with a +1.3 CPOE. Short throws (0-9) carry a +4 CPOE and positive EPA. He is a functional distributor on timing throws, and that skill is sustainable because it doesn't depend on protection holding for long.

strengths.title: Middle-of-field, intermediate windows
strengths.body: His best plays come between the numbers: 0.45 EPA over the middle and 0.253 on 10-19 yard throws. These are 17- and 20-attempt samples, so treat them as a hint. Still, at 6'6" he plainly sees and throws over the middle more comfortably than outside the hashes, where his EPA is negative to both sides.

strengths.title: Makai Lemon connection
strengths.body: Lemon has been his go-to target, drawing 23 targets at 0.204 EPA each, the best on the team. With Smith and Wicks out, that connection will carry even more of the passing game, for better or worse.

concerns.title: Sacks kill drives
concerns.body: He converts 31.3% of pressures into sacks and ranks 32nd of 49 in sack rate, despite a 2.65-second time to throw that isn't long. He isn't holding the ball to create; he rarely scrambles, at 3.9% of dropbacks. The pressure simply ends plays. A pace of 57 sacks is what turns his completion-rate competence into negative EPA.

concerns.title: No vertical threat
concerns.body: He is 0-for-8 on throws of 20+ air yards, with an interception and -11.5 total EPA. The small sample makes the exact number noisy. But with a 14.91% aggressiveness rate and a career-long bad-throw problem, defenses have little reason to respect the deep ball, which compresses everything underneath.

concerns.title: Persistent inaccuracy
concerns.body: His 17.5% bad-throw rate ranks 39th of 42, and he ranked near the bottom in both prior cameos. That is a trait, not a blip. It shows up most in one-score games, where his CPOE sinks to -7.5.

trend.note: His passing yards barely moved (215, 211, 212), and his EPA was negative in all three games. Week 8 at Washington was the worst of them, with 5 sacks, a lost fumble and -10.6 passing EPA.

nextGame.headline: Pittsburgh's pass rush meets the league's most sack-prone profile
nextGame.body:
If McKee plays, Pittsburgh is about the worst fit for him. The Steelers rank 6th in defensive EPA and 4th in sack rate, and they are stingy exactly where he lives: 8th in EPA allowed on short throws. Their weakness is deep, where they rank 23rd, but he hasn't completed a deep ball all season. The one soft spot he can attack is the tight end: Pittsburgh is 30th in EPA allowed to TE1s, which suits Dallas Goedert working the middle. Pittsburgh's offense also passes more than expected and leads the league in rushing EPA, a recipe for the Eagles' 27th-ranked defense to fall behind again. That would push him into the trailing-script volume that props up his completion rate.

Availability is the bigger story. McKee is listed as QB2 and was limited and questionable before Milton started Week 9, so he may not take the snaps at all. On his side, DeVonta Smith (87% of snaps) and Dontayvion Wicks (80%) are out with return dates of the game day itself, leaving Lemon and Goedert as the only proven options. Pittsburgh's absences — two depth corners, a rotational defensive tackle and receiver Michael Pittman Jr. — barely touch his matchup. The bye means 14 days of rest. No line has been posted.

keyMatchups.title: Protection versus a top-four sack rate
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh gets home on 8.2% of dropbacks, and McKee has turned 31.3% of pressures into sacks. This is where the game is decided: drive-ending sacks put him in third-and-long, where he is converting 28.6%.

keyMatchups.title: Goedert against a leaky TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh allows 0.45 EPA per play to tight ends, 30th in the league, while holding WR1s to -0.02. With the receiver room thinned, Goedert in the middle of the field is McKee's cleanest path to positive plays.

keyMatchups.title: Short game into a tight short defense
keyMatchups.body: His offense runs on throws under 10 yards, and Pittsburgh ranks 8th in short-pass EPA allowed. The deep shots they do allow are the throws he hasn't hit, so he has little room to work.

nextGame.watch: Who starts at quarterback. If it's McKee, watch whether the Eagles keep him in quick game and move the pocket to blunt Pittsburgh's rush.

restOfSeason.body:
His role is the first unknown. He is a QB2 behind an unsettled quarterback situation, coming off a limited-practice week. When he plays, expect the same shape: 35-40 attempts, a high completion rate on short throws and around 200 yards, with yardage propped up by trailing game scripts. Expect too many sacks and very little scoring. His 1.8% TD rate is low, but on this offense it isn't obviously unlucky.

The sack rate is the most likely thing to stay bad, since it has followed him with both a decent and a poor line. The deep-ball zero should improve slightly with volume, because nobody stays 0-for-forever. The interception rate (1.8%) is a bit kind given the bad-throw rate. Smith and Wicks returning would help more than anything in the scheme. Projections assume he starts.
swingFactors: Whether he or another QB gets the starts
Health of DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks

confidence.note: Three games, an uncertain QB role, his own injury status and a depleted receiver room.
